passages.text: Now in those days, when there was no king in Israel, a Levite who lived in the remote hill country of Ephraim took for himself a concubine from Bethlehem in Judah.
passages.sermon:
In those days, Israel had no king.
A Levite lived in the remote hill country of Ephraim.
This Levite took a concubine for himself.
The concubine came from Bethlehem in Judah.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֙ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם וּמֶ֖לֶךְ אֵ֣ין בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיְהִ֣י׀ אִ֣ישׁ לֵוִ֗י גָּ֚ר בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֣י הַר־ אֶפְרַ֔יִם וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ לוֹ֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה פִילֶ֔גֶשׁ מִבֵּ֥ית לֶ֖חֶם יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: But she was unfaithful to him and left him to return to her father’s house in Bethlehem in Judah. After she had been there four months, her husband got up and went after her to speak kindly to her and bring her back, taking his servant and a pair of donkeys. So the girl brought him into her father’s house, and when her father saw him, he gladly welcomed him.
passages.sermon:
In those days, there was no king in Israel.
A Levite lived in the remote hill country of Ephraim.
He took a concubine from Bethlehem in Judah.
The concubine was unfaithful to the Levite.
She left him.
She went to her father's house in Bethlehem in Judah.
She stayed there for four months.
After four months, her husband got up.
He went after her.
He wanted to speak kindly to her.
He wanted to bring her back.
He took his servant with him.
He took a pair of donkeys.
The girl brought him into her father's house.
Her father saw him.
Her father gladly welcomed him.
passages.original: וַתִּזְנֶ֤ה עָלָיו֙ פִּֽילַגְשׁ֔וֹ וַתֵּ֤לֶךְ מֵֽאִתּוֹ֙ אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יהָ אֶל־ בֵּ֥ית לֶ֖חֶם יְהוּדָ֑ה וַתְּהִי־ שָׁ֕ם יָמִ֖ים אַרְבָּעָ֥ה חֳדָשִֽׁים׃ וַיָּ֨קָם אִישָׁ֜הּ וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ אַחֲרֶ֗יהָ לְדַבֵּ֤ר עַל־ לִבָּהּ֙ לַהֲשִׁיבוֹ וְנַעֲר֥וֹ עִמּ֖וֹ וְצֶ֣מֶד חֲמֹרִ֑ים וַתְּבִיאֵ֙הוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יהָ וַיִּרְאֵ֙הוּ֙ אֲבִ֣י הַֽנַּעֲרָ֔ה וַיִּשְׂמַ֖ח לִקְרָאתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: His father-in-law, the girl’s father, persuaded him to stay, so he remained with him three days, eating, drinking, and lodging there.
passages.sermon:
The Levite visited his concubine’s father.
Her father was also his father-in-law.
The father-in-law persuaded the Levite to stay.
The Levite remained with him for three days.
They ate together.
They drank together.
They spent the nights there.
passages.original: וַיֶּחֱזַק־ בּ֤וֹ חֹֽתְנוֹ֙ אֲבִ֣י הַֽנַּעֲרָ֔ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב אִתּ֖וֹ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים וַיֹּאכְלוּ֙ וַיִּשְׁתּ֔וּ וַיָּלִ֖ינוּ שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: On the fourth day, they got up early in the morning and prepared to depart, but the girl’s father said to his son-in-law, “Refresh your heart with a morsel of bread, and then you can go.”
passages.sermon:
The man was the woman's husband.
The woman was his concubine.
They stayed at her father's house in Bethlehem in Judah.
On the fourth day, they woke up early in the morning.
The man got up to leave.
The girl's father spoke to his son-in-law.
He said, "Refresh your heart with a piece of bread."
He said, "After that, you can go."
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הָרְבִיעִ֔י וַיַּשְׁכִּ֥ימוּ בַבֹּ֖קֶר וַיָּ֣קָם לָלֶ֑כֶת וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אֲבִ֨י הַֽנַּעֲרָ֜ה אֶל־ חֲתָנ֗וֹ סְעָ֧ד לִבְּךָ֛ פַּת־ לֶ֖חֶם וְאַחַ֥ר תֵּלֵֽכוּ׃

passages.text: So they sat down and the two of them ate and drank together. Then the girl’s father said to the man, “Please agree to stay overnight and let your heart be merry.”
passages.sermon:
The man visited his father-in-law.  
His father-in-law was the girl's father.  
They both sat down together.  
They ate together.  
They drank together.  
The girl's father spoke to the man.  
He said, "Please stay here tonight."  
He said, "Let your heart be happy."
passages.original: וַיֵּשְׁב֗וּ וַיֹּאכְל֧וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֛ם יַחְדָּ֖ו וַיִּשְׁתּ֑וּ וַיֹּ֜אמֶר אֲבִ֤י הַֽנַּעֲרָה֙ אֶל־ הָאִ֔ישׁ הֽוֹאֶל־ נָ֥א וְלִ֖ין וְיִטַ֥ב לִבֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: The man got up to depart, but his father-in-law persuaded him, so he stayed there that night.
passages.sermon:
A man was visiting his father-in-law.
The man got up to leave.
His father-in-law spoke to him.
His father-in-law urged him to stay.
The man listened to his father-in-law.
The man stayed there that night.
passages.original: וַיָּ֥קָם הָאִ֖ישׁ לָלֶ֑כֶת וַיִּפְצַר־ בּוֹ֙ חֹתְנ֔וֹ וַיָּ֖שָׁב וַיָּ֥לֶן שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: On the fifth day, he got up early in the morning to depart, but the girl’s father said, “Please refresh your heart.” So they waited until late afternoon and the two of them ate.
passages.sermon:
The man got up early in the morning on the fifth day.
He planned to leave.
The girl's father spoke to him.
The girl's father said, "Please refresh your heart."
They waited until the day was far spent.
The man and the girl's father ate together.
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם בַּבֹּ֜קֶר בַּיּ֣וֹם הַחֲמִישִׁי֮ לָלֶכֶת֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀ אֲבִ֣י הַֽנַּעֲרָ֗ה סְעָד־ נָא֙ לְבָ֣בְךָ֔ וְהִֽתְמַהְמְה֖וּ עַד־ נְט֣וֹת הַיּ֑וֹם וַיֹּאכְל֖וּ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: When the man got up to depart with his concubine and his servant, his father-in-law, the girl’s father, said to him, “Look, the day is drawing to a close. Please spend the night. See, the day is almost over. Spend the night here, that your heart may be merry. Then you can get up early tomorrow for your journey home.”
passages.sermon:
A man prepared to leave.
He had his concubine with him.
He also had his servant with him.
The girl’s father was his father-in-law.
The father-in-law spoke to the man.
He said, “Look, the day is ending.”
He said, “Please stay the night.”
He said, “See, the day is almost over.”
He said, “Stay here tonight.”
He said, “Let your heart be glad.”
He said, “In the morning, get up early.”
He said, “Then you can travel on your way.”
He said, “You can go home tomorrow.”
passages.original: וַיָּ֤קָם הָאִישׁ֙ לָלֶ֔כֶת ה֥וּא וּפִילַגְשׁ֖וֹ וְנַעֲר֑וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֣וֹ חֹתְנ֣וֹ אֲבִ֣י הַֽנַּעֲרָ֡ה הִנֵּ֣ה נָא֩ רָפָ֨ה הַיּ֜וֹם לַעֲרֹ֗ב לִֽינוּ־ נָ֞א הִנֵּ֨ה חֲנ֤וֹת הַיּוֹם֙ לִ֥ין פֹּה֙ וְיִיטַ֣ב לְבָבֶ֔ךָ וְהִשְׁכַּמְתֶּ֤ם מָחָר֙ לְדַרְכְּכֶ֔ם וְהָלַכְתָּ֖ לְאֹהָלֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: But the man was unwilling to spend the night. He got up and departed, and arrived opposite Jebus (that is, Jerusalem), with his two saddled donkeys and his concubine.
passages.sermon:
The man did not want to spend the night.
He got up.
He left.
He came to a place across from Jebus.
Jebus is Jerusalem.
He had two donkeys with him.
The donkeys were saddled.
His concubine was with him.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ אָבָ֤ה הָאִישׁ֙ לָל֔וּן וַיָּ֣קָם וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ וַיָּבֹא֙ עַד־ נֹ֣כַח יְב֔וּס הִ֖יא יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְעִמּ֗וֹ צֶ֤מֶד חֲמוֹרִים֙ חֲבוּשִׁ֔ים וּפִילַגְשׁ֖וֹ עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When they were near Jebus and the day was almost gone, the servant said to his master, “Please, let us stop at this Jebusite city and spend the night here.”
passages.sermon:
A man traveled with his concubine and his servant.
They came near the city of Jebus.
Jebus is also called Jerusalem.
The day was almost over.
The servant spoke to his master.
The servant said, “Please, let us turn aside to this Jebusite city.
Let us spend the night here.”
passages.original: הֵ֣ם עִם־ יְב֔וּס וְהַיּ֖וֹם רַ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַנַּ֜עַר אֶל־ אֲדֹנָ֗יו לְכָה־ נָּ֛א וְנָס֛וּרָה אֶל־ עִֽיר־ הַיְבוּסִ֥י הַזֹּ֖את וְנָלִ֥ין בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: But his master replied, “We will not turn aside to the city of foreigners, where there are no Israelites. We will go on to Gibeah.”
passages.sermon:
The master was a Levite man traveling with his servant, his concubine, and two donkeys.
The servant suggested they stop in the city of Jebus, which belonged to foreigners, not Israelites.
The master answered his servant.
He said, "We will not turn aside to a foreign city."
He said, "This city does not belong to the people of Israel."
He said, "We will continue on our journey."
He said, "We will go to Gibeah instead."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ אֲדֹנָ֔יו לֹ֤א נָסוּר֙ אֶל־ עִ֣יר נָכְרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־ מִבְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵ֑נָּה וְעָבַ֖רְנוּ עַד־ גִּבְעָֽה׃

passages.text: He continued, “Come, let us try to reach one of these towns to spend the night in Gibeah or Ramah.”
passages.sermon:
A Levite traveled with his servant.
The Levite spoke to his servant.
He said, “Let us go on.”
He said, “Let us come near one of these places.”
He said, “We can spend the night in Gibeah.”
He said, “Or we can spend the night in Ramah.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְנַעֲר֔וֹ לְךָ֥ וְנִקְרְבָ֖ה בְּאַחַ֣ד הַמְּקֹמ֑וֹת וְלַ֥נּוּ בַגִּבְעָ֖ה א֥וֹ בָרָמָֽה׃

passages.text: So they continued on their journey, and the sun set as they neared Gibeah in Benjamin.
passages.sermon:
A group of travelers continued on their journey.
They walked along the road.
The sun began to set.
They came near the town of Gibeah.
Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
passages.original: וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ וַיֵּלֵ֑כוּ וַתָּבֹ֤א לָהֶם֙ הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ אֵ֥צֶל הַגִּבְעָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְבִנְיָמִֽן׃

passages.text: They stopped to go in and lodge in Gibeah. The Levite went in and sat down in the city square, but no one would take them into his home for the night.
passages.sermon:
The Levite and his companions stopped in Gibeah.
They wanted to spend the night there.
The Levite entered the city.
He sat down in the city square.
No one in Gibeah invited them into a house for the night.
passages.original: וַיָּסֻ֣רוּ שָׁ֔ם לָב֖וֹא לָל֣וּן בַּגִּבְעָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֗א וַיֵּ֙שֶׁב֙ בִּרְח֣וֹב הָעִ֔יר וְאֵ֥ין אִ֛ישׁ מְאַסֵּֽף־ אוֹתָ֥ם הַבַּ֖יְתָה לָלֽוּן׃

passages.text: That evening an old man from the hill country of Ephraim, who was residing in Gibeah (the men of that place were Benjamites), came in from his work in the field.
passages.sermon:
An old man came in from his work in the field.
This happened in the evening.
The old man was from the hill country of Ephraim.
He was living in Gibeah.
The people of Gibeah were Benjamites.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֣ה׀ אִ֣ישׁ זָקֵ֗ן בָּ֣א מִֽן־ מַעֲשֵׂ֤הוּ מִן־ הַשָּׂדֶה֙ בָּעֶ֔רֶב וְהָאִישׁ֙ מֵהַ֣ר אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְהוּא־ גָ֖ר בַּגִּבְעָ֑ה וְאַנְשֵׁ֥י הַמָּק֖וֹם בְּנֵ֥י יְמִינִֽי׃

passages.text: When he looked up and saw the traveler in the city square, the old man asked, “Where are you going, and where have you come from?”
passages.sermon:
An old man lived in Gibeah.
He came from the hill country of Ephraim.
He was not a native of Gibeah.
The people of Gibeah were Benjamites.
The old man returned from his work in the field in the evening.
He looked up.
He saw a traveler sitting in the city square.
The old man spoke to the traveler.
He asked, "Where are you going?"
He also asked, "Where have you come from?"
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂ֣א עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּ֛רְא אֶת־ הָאִ֥ישׁ הָאֹרֵ֖חַ בִּרְחֹ֣ב הָעִ֑יר וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הָאִ֧ישׁ הַזָּקֵ֛ן אָ֥נָה תֵלֵ֖ךְ וּמֵאַ֥יִן תָּבֽוֹא׃

passages.text: The Levite replied, “We are traveling from Bethlehem in Judah to the remote hill country of Ephraim, where I am from. I went to Bethlehem in Judah, and now I am going to the house of the LORD; but no one has taken me into his home, even though there is both straw and feed for our donkeys, and bread and wine for me and the maidservant and young man with me. There is nothing that we, your servants, lack.”
passages.sermon:
The Levite spoke to the old man.
He said, “We are travelers.
We came from Bethlehem in Judah.
We are going to the far side of the hill country of Ephraim.
I am from that place.
I went to Bethlehem in Judah.
Now I am going to the house of the LORD.
No one has invited me into his home.
We have straw and feed for our donkeys.
We have bread and wine for me.
We have bread and wine for your maidservant.
We have bread and wine for the young man with your servants.
We do not lack anything.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו עֹבְרִ֨ים אֲנַ֜חְנוּ מִבֵּֽית־ לֶ֣חֶם יְהוּדָה֮ עַד־ יַרְכְּתֵ֣י הַר־ אֶפְרַיִם֒ מִשָּׁ֣ם אָנֹ֔כִי וָאֵלֵ֕ךְ עַד־ בֵּ֥ית לֶ֖חֶם יְהוּדָ֑ה וְאֶת־ בֵּ֤ית יְהוָה֙ אֲנִ֣י הֹלֵ֔ךְ וְאֵ֣ין אִ֔ישׁ מְאַסֵּ֥ף אוֹתִ֖י הַבָּֽיְתָה׃ וְגַם־ תֶּ֤בֶן גַּם־ מִסְפּוֹא֙ יֵ֣שׁ לַחֲמוֹרֵ֔ינוּ וְ֠גַם לֶ֣חֶם וָיַ֤יִן יֶשׁ־ לִי֙ וְלַֽאֲמָתֶ֔ךָ וְלַנַּ֖עַר עִם־ עֲבָדֶ֑יךָ אֵ֥ין מַחְס֖וֹר כָּל־ דָּבָֽר׃

passages.text: “Peace to you,” said the old man. “Let me supply everything you need. Only do not spend the night in the square.”
passages.sermon:
The old man spoke.
He said, "Peace to you."
He said, "I will supply everything you need."
He said, "Do not spend the night in the square."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הָאִ֤ישׁ הַזָּקֵן֙ שָׁל֣וֹם לָ֔ךְ רַ֥ק כָּל־ מַחְסוֹרְךָ֖ עָלָ֑י רַ֥ק בָּרְח֖וֹב אַל־ תָּלַֽן׃

passages.text: So he brought him to his house and fed his donkeys. And they washed their feet and ate and drank.
passages.sermon:
The old man brought the Levite into his house.
The old man gave food to the Levite’s donkeys.
The Levite and his companions washed their feet.
They ate.
They drank.
passages.original: וַיְבִיאֵ֣הוּ לְבֵית֔וֹ וַיָּ֖בָול לַחֲמוֹרִ֑ים וַֽיִּרְחֲצוּ֙ רַגְלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּאכְל֖וּ וַיִּשְׁתּֽוּ׃

passages.text: While they were enjoying themselves, suddenly the wicked men of the city surrounded the house. Pounding on the door, they said to the old man who owned the house, “Bring out the man who came to your house, so we can have relations with him!”
passages.sermon:
The old man owned the house.
He had welcomed a guest into his home.
The guest was a Levite traveler.
The Levite was staying with the old man for the night.
The Levite was not from the city.
The old man and his guests were eating and drinking.
They were enjoying themselves inside the house.
Suddenly, wicked men from the city arrived.
These men were called sons of Belial.
They were evil and lawless.
They surrounded the house.
They began to pound on the door.
They shouted to the old man, the owner of the house.
They said, “Bring out the man who came to your house.”
They wanted to have relations with him.
passages.original: הֵמָּה֮ מֵיטִיבִ֣ים אֶת־ לִבָּם֒ וְהִנֵּה֩ אַנְשֵׁ֨י הָעִ֜יר אַנְשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי־ בְלִיַּ֗עַל נָסַ֙בּוּ֙ אֶת־ הַבַּ֔יִת מִֽתְדַּפְּקִ֖ים עַל־ הַדָּ֑לֶת וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ אֶל־ הָ֠אִישׁ בַּ֣עַל הַבַּ֤יִת הַזָּקֵן֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הוֹצֵ֗א אֶת־ הָאִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֥א אֶל־ בֵּיתְךָ֖ וְנֵדָעֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: The owner of the house went out and said to them, “No, my brothers, do not do this wicked thing! After all, this man is a guest in my house. Do not commit this outrage.
passages.sermon:
The owner of the house was an old man.
He went out to the men of the city.
He spoke to them directly.
He said, “No, my brothers.
Do not do this evil thing.
This man is a guest in my house.
Do not commit this outrage.”
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֣א אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם הָאִישׁ֙ בַּ֣עַל הַבַּ֔יִת וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אַל־ אַחַ֖י אַל־ תָּרֵ֣עוּ נָ֑א אַ֠חֲרֵי אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֞א הָאִ֤ישׁ הַזֶּה֙ אַל־ בֵּיתִ֔י אַֽל־ תַּעֲשׂ֖וּ אֶת־ הַנְּבָלָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: Look, let me bring out my virgin daughter and the man’s concubine, and you can use them and do with them as you wish. But do not do such a vile thing to this man.”
passages.sermon:
The old man owned the house.
He spoke to the wicked men of the city.
He said, “Look, here is my virgin daughter.
Here is the visitor’s concubine.
I will bring them out to you.
You may mistreat them.
You may do to them what seems good to you.
But do not do this vile thing to this man.”
passages.original: הִנֵּה֩ בִתִּ֨י הַבְּתוּלָ֜ה וּפִֽילַגְשֵׁ֗הוּ אוֹצִֽיאָה־ נָּ֤א אוֹתָם֙ וְעַנּ֣וּ אוֹתָ֔ם וַעֲשׂ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ם הַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֑ם וְלָאִ֤ישׁ הַזֶּה֙ לֹ֣א תַעֲשׂ֔וּ דְּבַ֖ר הַנְּבָלָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: But the men would not listen to him. So the Levite took his concubine and sent her outside to them, and they raped her and abused her throughout the night, and at dawn they let her go.
passages.sermon:
The men stood outside the house.
They refused to listen to the owner of the house.
The Levite was the woman's master.
The Levite took his concubine.
He sent his concubine outside to the men.
The men seized the concubine.
They raped her all night.
They abused her until morning.
At dawn, the men let her go.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ אָב֤וּ הָאֲנָשִׁים֙ לִשְׁמֹ֣עַֽ ל֔וֹ וַיַּחֲזֵ֤ק הָאִישׁ֙ בְּפִ֣ילַגְשׁ֔וֹ וַיֹּצֵ֥א אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם הַח֑וּץ וַיֵּדְע֣וּ א֠וֹתָהּ וַיִּֽתְעַלְּלוּ־ בָ֤הּ כָּל־ הַלַּ֙יְלָה֙ עַד־ הַבֹּ֔קֶר וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֖וּהָ בַּעֲלוֹת הַשָּֽׁחַר׃

passages.text: Early that morning, the woman went back to the house where her master was staying, collapsed at the doorway, and lay there until it was light.
passages.sermon:
A woman was a concubine.
Men abused her all night.
Early in the morning, the woman returned.
She went to the house where her master stayed.
She collapsed at the doorway of the house.
She lay there until daylight.
passages.original: וַתָּבֹ֥א הָאִשָּׁ֖ה לִפְנ֣וֹת הַבֹּ֑קֶר וַתִּפֹּ֞ל פֶּ֧תַח בֵּית־ הָאִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ אֲדוֹנֶ֥יהָ שָּׁ֖ם עַד־ הָאֽוֹר׃

passages.text: In the morning, when her master got up and opened the doors of the house to go out on his journey, there was his concubine, collapsed in the doorway of the house, with her hands on the threshold.
passages.sermon:
The Levite was the woman's master.
He got up in the morning.
He opened the doors of the house.
He went out to begin his journey.
He saw his concubine.
She was lying at the doorway of the house.
Her hands were on the threshold.
passages.original: וַיָּ֨קָם אֲדֹנֶ֜יהָ בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַיִּפְתַּח֙ דַּלְת֣וֹת הַבַּ֔יִת וַיֵּצֵ֖א לָלֶ֣כֶת לְדַרְכּ֑וֹ וְהִנֵּ֧ה הָאִשָּׁ֣ה פִֽילַגְשׁ֗וֹ נֹפֶ֙לֶת֙ פֶּ֣תַח הַבַּ֔יִת וְיָדֶ֖יהָ עַל־ הַסַּֽף׃

passages.text: “Get up,” he told her. “Let us go.” But there was no response. So the man put her on his donkey and set out for home.
passages.sermon:
The man was her master.
He spoke to the woman.
He said, “Get up.”
He said, “Let us go.”
She did not answer.
She gave no response.
The man lifted her onto his donkey.
The man got up.
He went to his home.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלֶ֛יהָ ק֥וּמִי וְנֵלֵ֖כָה וְאֵ֣ין עֹנֶ֑ה וַיִּקָּחֶ֙הָ֙ עַֽל־ הַחֲמ֔וֹר וַיָּ֣קָם הָאִ֔ישׁ וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ לִמְקֹמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When he reached his house, he picked up a knife, took hold of his concubine, cut her limb by limb into twelve pieces, and sent her throughout the territory of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The man was a Levite.
He returned to his house.
He picked up a knife.
He took hold of his concubine.
He cut her body into twelve pieces.
He sent the twelve pieces throughout all the territory of Israel.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֣א אֶל־ בֵּית֗וֹ וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת־ הַֽמַּאֲכֶ֙לֶת֙ וַיַּחֲזֵ֣ק בְּפִֽילַגְשׁ֔וֹ וַֽיְנַתְּחֶ֙הָ֙ לַעֲצָמֶ֔יהָ לִשְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר נְתָחִ֑ים וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֶ֔הָ בְּכֹ֖ל גְּב֥וּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And everyone who saw it said, “Nothing like this has been seen or done from the day the Israelites came out of the land of Egypt until this day. Think it over, take counsel, and speak up!”
passages.sermon:
Everyone who saw what happened spoke.
They said, “Nothing like this has ever happened before.
No one has seen or done such a thing.
This has not happened since the Israelites left Egypt.
This is true up to this very day.
Think about what has happened.
Decide what to do.
Speak out.”
passages.original: וְהָיָ֣ה כָל־ הָרֹאֶ֗ה וְאָמַר֙ לֹֽא־ נִהְיְתָ֤ה וְלֹֽא־ נִרְאֲתָה֙ כָּזֹ֔את לְמִיּ֞וֹם עֲל֤וֹת בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה שִֽׂימוּ־ לָכֶ֥ם עָלֶ֖יהָ עֻ֥צוּ וְדַבֵּֽרוּ׃פ
